lark_e05_entry.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry.text: The appendix keeper lived over the eastern stair, in a room whose doorway had worn into a slant. On Day Thirty Five, Lin arrived with Chen Rui at the agreed hour. Qin had declined the invitation; his freight booking had become an actual morning job, and the job mattered more than hearing a supplier explain itself. Shan Fang wished them a useful argument and stayed with her own lesson group. Lin brought the meeting notice and her notebook. Chen brought the sealed drawing, a small sample joint, and his client's written request.

lark_e05_entry_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_002.text: The keeper's name was Hu Lan. She had worked at the freight desk before the association kept a bound appendix, and she remembered why its first loose pages had been tied together. A supplier had copied a working joint while omitting the limit that made it safe. The copy looked cleaner than the original and failed under the very load for which the limit existed. Hu Lan did not tell the story to forbid every comparison. She set the old failed drawing on the table and asked them what they intended to compare.

lark_e05_entry_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_003.text: Chen's client had made a joint whose stop rested outside the signal housing. A worker could see it without opening the cover. The client's written claim concerned access for inspection and replacement, not a stronger bell or a more advanced cultivator. Chen put the sample on the table, where its wooden base prevented anybody from mistaking it for an installed fitting. He asked permission to explain how the stop was supposed to behave. Hu Lan gave that permission for the sample's own method. She did not yet open the association's appendix.

lark_e05_entry_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_004.text: The external stop could be moved with a small ordinary tool. Chen demonstrated its travel against the unpowered wooden base. At the far end, the stop pushed the cover into a position that exposed a red line. He called the line an inspection warning. Lin asked whether a loose cover could expose it when the stop had not moved. Chen loosened a screw, tried the movement, and found that it could. He wrote the result on his client's copy of the drawing. A warning had acquired an additional possible cause before any association secret appeared.

lark_e05_entry_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_005.text: Hu Lan asked what the client wanted in return for showing the sample. Chen read the paragraph rather than softening it. The client wanted a reserved comparison session and access to the freight appendix's joint dimensions. It hoped to sell a replacement fitting afterward. Hu Lan said a sale was not her promise to make. The association could authorize a comparison within limits; the actual freight crew would still need to receive a successful installation proposal. Chen accepted the distinction and turned the sample so its loosened screw remained visible.

lark_e05_entry_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_006.text: Lin had seen the bell room's comparison strip but had not learned this joint's internal design. She said so. Chen did not need her to pretend expertise to make the meeting worthwhile. He wanted someone who could separate a visible observation from a confident story about its cause. Hu Lan wanted the same thing for a different reason. Between them, Lin found a useful place that did not require being either a supplier's champion or a keeper's trusted replacement. She could ask a question and show exactly what led her to it.

lark_e05_entry_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_007.text: The appendix belonged to the association. Freight workers had supplied the timings and corrections; former keepers had written instructions; several commercial drawings remained licensed for this local use. Lin's employment gave her the pages needed for her assigned work. It did not transfer the other authors' permissions into her hands. Hu Lan showed the public contents list. The evacuation instructions were available to anybody using the stair. The internal geometry of the signal housing sat in a separate section, beside restrictions that differed from drawing to drawing.

lark_e05_entry_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_008.text: Chen's client had included a request to photograph nothing, because it had no photographic apparatus, and to make a dimension copy in ink instead. The prohibition against taking the book away was easy to satisfy. The proposed ink copy was the actual issue. Hu Lan marked its paragraph with a plain wooden pointer. A visitor could look at a page and still carry away its dimensions in a notebook. They would need a permission that named the information, the permitted use, and what could leave the room. Calling the meeting an observation would not settle those questions.

lark_e05_entry_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_009.text: Hu Lan could offer three forms of participation for Lin. In a restricted session, Lin could inspect the authorized joint section beside the keeper and work as the association's comparison recorder; her private notes would remain in the room, and she would owe a received report before the visiting board met on Day Fifty Four. In a public session, she could test only a published inspection jig and release the ordinary observations. She could also decline both sessions, leaving the supplier and qualified crew to conduct their own business without her contribution.

lark_e05_entry_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_010.text: The restricted session offered detail that might later help her understand why a particular warning failed. It also took two free afternoons and made her responsible for a narrow, useful report. The public session let household readers use the results immediately but could not answer questions that depended on the hidden housing dimensions. Declining freed the two afternoons for a promised grain sellers' meeting at the lower market. That meeting concerned a leaking storage roof, and its organizer had already asked Lin to read disputed delivery dates. None of the three appointments could be completed by attending another one.

lark_e05_entry_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_011.text: Lin asked why the two comparison sessions occupied the same afternoons. The qualified fitting crew could attend only those dates before returning to its other jobs. Hu Lan had no reason to reserve the crew twice for the same request. The grain sellers met when their travelling carrier was physically in town. She had been asked to help there, but had not accepted. Chen said his client's comparison would proceed under whichever competent people the association chose. Lin's refusal would not make the sample vanish or leave the freight line automatically unsafe.

lark_e05_entry_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_012.text: The association would pay the qualified crew from its ordinary operating account, distinct from Lin's instruction appropriation. The supplier would pay Chen's agreed presentation fee from its own funds. Lin's two afternoons, if accepted, would be an unpaid professional observation outside her existing shifts, with the limits read aloud before she consented. Hu Lan was willing to explain that unromantic part clearly. Useful access could come with work. Lin could judge the offered work without pretending that access was wages or that curiosity made her time free.

lark_e05_entry_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_013.text: Hu Lan passed her the three written invitations. One had a blank for the restricted report's receiving date. One had a blank naming where the public jig observations would be posted. The third simply recorded that Lin had declined participation and would receive no confidential section. Chen waited without recommending the form that best served his client. Lin appreciated the restraint more because it had probably cost him an easy sentence. Through the open shutter, a cart wheel struck the same uneven stair joint three times in slow succession.

lark_e05_entry_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_014.text: Lin thought of the child's turnip hound, the shrine room's cap molds, and the old drawing whose neatness had concealed its dangerous omission. She could not choose every useful task by imagining that tomorrow would contain more hours. Her work shift on Day Thirty Six and the clinician's exercises already occupied their proper places. The two offered afternoons remained available, but only once. She laid her palm on the table instead of gripping the nearest paper. Hu Lan waited until Lin had read each invitation through to its last line.

lark_e05_entry_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_entry_015.text: Chen took a drink of water while the keeper sorted the client drawings. He seemed less like a man carrying a solution than a man carrying a conversation between people who had reasons to mistrust one another. Lin had travelled with messages often enough to recognize the weight. She also recognized the temptation to reward a friend's effort with agreement. He had brought the sample honestly. She owed him an honest answer, which could still leave his preferred appointment unfilled. The sample's red warning line remained exposed above the loosened screw.

lark_e05_access_choice.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_choice.text: Hu Lan held the invitations apart so no signature could drift from one set of terms into another. The restricted pages, the public jig, and the grain meeting would give Lin different people to answer to and different facts she could later use. The two free afternoons would be spent in one place. She had heard the costs and the limits. Now she chose the work she would actually attend.

choices.text: Accept restricted comparison access and deliver its bounded report.
Choose the public jig session and publish its ordinary observations.
Decline the comparison and accept the grain sellers' meeting.

lark_e05_access_restricted.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted.text: Lin accepted the restricted recorder's role. Hu Lan read the report date aloud, and Lin repeated Day Fifty Four before signing. The keeper gave her a numbered practice notebook that would stay in the appendix room. Chen could explain his client's sample there but could not ask her to send the notebook to the client. Lin sent an ordinary refusal to the grain meeting's organizer that afternoon, before anyone counted on her arrival. Her free time had become work with a receiving place, and another invitation had become a closed possibility.

lark_e05_access_restricted_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_002.text: The first comparison took place on Day Thirty Seven. The qualified fitting crew brought an unused housing to the keeper's bench. It was empty of powered parts and fixed to a wooden block. Hu Lan opened only the authorized section beside it. Lin could see why the older method hid its stop: a shield against grit also obscured the inspection line. A worker using the public drawing would know to check the cover but would not know the exact space behind it. That additional fact entered the room notebook and remained there.

lark_e05_access_restricted_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_003.text: The crew measured the sample against its own drawing before comparing it with the old housing. One hole had wandered slightly from the declared position. The discrepancy was small enough that Chen first blamed the table's uneven light. A fitter turned the sample, measured again, and found the same offset. Chen wrote it into his client's correction sheet. Lin wrote both the result and the repeated method in the restricted record. Her work did not consist of choosing which man looked more embarrassed. It consisted of leaving a comparison they could repeat.

lark_e05_access_restricted_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_004.text: The offset mattered because the exposed stop's warning line appeared before the fitting reached the position named in the supplier's instruction. It was not yet an accident. The crew had caught it on a powerless bench. Chen asked whether the warning instruction could be altered to match the sample. The fitter said a drawing could describe one imperfect object accurately without proving that the next manufactured object would share its imperfection. Lin had never thought a faithful correction could be inadequate in that way. She left the original drawing beside the corrected sheet.

lark_e05_access_restricted_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_005.text: Hu Lan permitted the supplier to carry away its own measurements and the association's decision to postpone any installation. The internal clearance comparison remained under the appendix's local license. Lin could report publicly that no new fitting had been installed and that the bench comparison had found an unresolved manufacturing discrepancy. She could not publish the private dimensions to make that conclusion more impressive. Chen read the public sentence and accepted it. His client would be disappointed, but it would receive a useful defect rather than an invented sale.

lark_e05_access_restricted_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_006.text: On Day Thirty Nine, the second session used a properly remade sample brought from the client's travelling stock. The crew checked its holes first. This time the warning line appeared at the stated place in every repeated unpowered movement. Grit gathered under the external lip during a separate dry test, however, and cleaning it required a narrower tool than the proposed household inspection kit contained. The sample was promising under revised service terms. It was not a thing an ordinary passerby could be told to maintain with any available knife.

lark_e05_access_restricted_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_007.text: Lin's report distinguished the two samples by their stamped numbers. Combining their best features would have described an object nobody had brought into the room. Hu Lan pointed out where Lin had written that the second sample was easier to clean. Easier for whom? Lin added the qualified fitter's tool and the fixed bench position. She had earned a question she could use again, and an obligation to state its answer exactly here. Her notebook remained in the keeper's cupboard when the afternoon ended.

lark_e05_access_restricted_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_restricted_008.text: Chen walked with her as far as the lower stair. He thanked her for recording the first sample's fault without treating it as proof of dishonesty. She thanked him for accepting the measurement before it became a personal argument. Neither thanked the other for an outcome that had not yet happened. His client still had to decide whether the revised tool requirement fit its offer. Lin still owed the received report on Day Fifty Four. The evening wind turned the market's hanging aprons outward, making every empty doorway look briefly occupied.

lark_e05_access_public.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public.text: Lin accepted the public jig session. Hu Lan wrote the market's lower notice board into the receiving form, then gave her a copy of the published inspection method. The closed joint section stayed closed. Chen would explain only the visible sample and its public claims at her session. Lin sent a timely refusal to the grain meeting organizer, who had not yet booked her help. She could not make this choice seem more generous by quietly promising that other meeting an hour she had already given away.

lark_e05_access_public_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_002.text: The first session on Day Thirty Seven used a wooden jig with no housing dimensions concealed inside it. Household readers stood around the bench beside a qualified fitter. The fitter showed where ordinary pressure on the cover could expose the sample's red warning line without moving its stop. Chen repeated the demonstration and agreed to amend his client's public description. The line could tell a reader to seek an inspection. It could not, on its own, name the fault or authorize continued use. Lin wrote that distinction in large enough script for the back row.

lark_e05_access_public_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_003.text: One of the household readers was the woman who sold onions above the cart stair. She asked whether a cover that hid the line must therefore be safe. Chen began to answer from the sample's intended design. The fitter stopped him and showed a deliberately obstructed jig movement. Its cover hid the line while its stop failed to reach the proper position. The seller nodded with no sign of triumph. She had to pass the bell's stair with her children; a false reassurance interested her more than an argument won against a visitor.

lark_e05_access_public_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_004.text: Lin drew the two visible situations without claiming they described every possible failure inside an installed housing. The public method had a useful boundary: see the changed line, report it, keep to the posted route instructions. A household reader was not asked to open the powered signal equipment. Hu Lan received Lin's first draft at the end of the afternoon. She asked Lin to remove a phrase that made the red line sound like a diagnosis. The erased words left more room for a plain instruction that readers could carry uphill.

lark_e05_access_public_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_005.text: The onion seller repeated Lin's corrected sentence to a man who had missed the demonstration. He turned it into a claim that the new fitting had already been installed. She corrected him before he passed it farther. Lin saw how quickly a modest comparison could acquire an imaginary object and an imaginary date. She added the sample's present bench location to the public heading. Everybody could go and find what had actually been shown. The seller read the heading once more, then asked for a copy her sister could keep.

lark_e05_access_public_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_006.text: The second session on Day Thirty Nine tested whether readers could find the heading from the crowded stair. Hu Lan permitted the market board's keeper to shift it away from a hanging apron that obscured the first line. A child read the sample's bench location correctly but mistook the instruction to report a changed warning for permission to test it. Lin put the reporting verb before the illustration. When the child read it again, he went to the actual keeper instead of reaching toward the model. The revision had changed a small action.

lark_e05_access_public_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_007.text: Chen received the public observations on his client's behalf. They answered the visible warning claim and the ordinary reader's task, but left the appendix's internal clearance question unanswered. His client would need a separate restricted comparison if it still wanted that fact. Lin did not have the private dimensions to offer during an informal conversation. The missing knowledge was a real limit of the choice she had accepted. In exchange, the onion seller could carry home a permitted copy whose practical instruction had survived a crowded stair and a skeptical question.

lark_e05_access_public_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_public_008.text: Lin placed the final public sheet in the board keeper's hands for the dated posting. The keeper signed its receiving line and gave her the ordinary acknowledgment that Hu Lan would later use for the session record. Nobody owed a confidential report from her. She kept a copy of her own authorized public drawing and took it to Qin's household. His daughter liked the red warning line and wanted to draw it on her turnip hound. Lin let her copy the color and explained that an animal was permitted to remain only an animal.

lark_e05_access_grain.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain.text: Lin declined the comparison work and accepted the grain sellers' invitation instead. Hu Lan closed the access forms without opening the confidential appendix. Chen would make his client's presentation to the qualified crew without Lin as recorder. The keeper gave her the public notice of the proposed comparison, so she would not mistake declining a role for being forbidden to know that a meeting existed. Lin sent her acceptance to the grain organizer and received the two afternoon dates in reply. Those hours now belonged to an entirely different argument.

lark_e05_access_grain_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_002.text: On Day Thirty Seven, the grain sellers gathered beneath a storage roof that had leaked through two spring deliveries. The travelling carrier brought his own receiving slips. The sellers had accused him of leaving sacks in the weather after claiming timely delivery. He said the room had already been wet. Lin laid the slips in date order and asked where each sack had been placed before anybody guessed who was lying. The room's keeper remembered shifting a bench between the two deliveries. That ordinary movement gave the papers a new question to answer.

lark_e05_access_grain_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_003.text: The carrier's first delivery had been received on the dry bench. The second had been received after the bench was moved beneath a visible roof crack. The papers did not say that the second cargo had been dry, only that its count matched the receiving list. Lin could not find a signed condition inspection for that load. The organizer disliked the gap. So did the carrier. They had treated a count receipt as if it also settled the grain's condition, and its neat total had concealed the very thing they now wished to prove.

lark_e05_access_grain_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_004.text: A seller offered to swear that every sack had been dry when she helped stack it. Another remembered dampness but could not say whether it came from the room or the road. Lin wrote both recollections beside the actual dates and left their disagreement visible. The sellers did not leave with an agreed story about the past. They left with an agreement to inspect the next arriving load at receiving, while the carrier and room keeper were both present. It was less satisfying than being vindicated and more likely to stop another argument before it grew.

lark_e05_access_grain_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_005.text: The roof repair raised a separate dispute. The keeper could patch the crack only if the sellers cleared the space beneath it for a morning. They feared leaving the sacks outside. The carrier offered his empty cart for covered storage during the work, at a named short hire that the organizer accepted from the sellers' own repair purse. Qin's cart was not secretly volunteered because Lin knew him. The carrier's offer did not amend the disputed old delivery. It supplied a present place for present sacks, and the room keeper accepted the repair morning.

lark_e05_access_grain_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_006.text: Lin returned on Day Thirty Nine. The sellers moved their sacks onto the agreed covered cart before the roof worker climbed to the crack. She stayed below with the receiving lists and kept people from treating departure into temporary storage as a sale. The worker found an old patch whose lower edge had been turned uphill. Rain could creep underneath it even when the upper seal looked good. That result concerned a roof, not a cultivator's channels, but Lin recognized the temptation to inspect only the face that made the repairer look competent.

lark_e05_access_grain_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_007.text: The keeper received the completed roof patch after a controlled ordinary water test. The sellers received their sacks back from the cart and inspected the condition while the carrier stood beside them. Two already damaged sacks were marked from the earlier disputed stock. They did not become new transport losses because the present inspection finally made them visible. Lin wrote a short record for the organizer and received thanks without wages; she had accepted the two afternoons as unpaid help. The old liability remained unresolved wherever the earlier evidence remained inadequate.

lark_e05_access_grain_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_access_grain_008.text: At supper, Chen told her the association's qualified crew had postponed his client's installation request after finding a manufacturing discrepancy on the bench. Lin had not seen the comparison and did not pretend to know its measurements. He could share the public decision, not the appendix's dimensions. She told him about the room's corrected roof and its still disputed grain. He thought the two meetings had been unusually similar for things so different. Lin said people wanted a clean ending before they had looked under the patch. He accepted the criticism even where it might apply to him.

lark_e05_after_001.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_001.text: The two afternoons ended with different work behind Lin, and Day Forty arrived without lending her a third one. Her accepted ordinary shift on Day Thirty Six had been completed and received between the invitation and the first appointment; its four copper had brought her earned wages to twenty. Now she returned for the sixth scheduled shift. At the noon rest, the receiving keeper asked whether the extra afternoon work had left her fit for the ordinary limits she had accepted. She reported her present fatigue instead of answering with the usefulness of the meetings.

lark_e05_after_002.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_002.text: The keeper moved one prolonged seated task earlier in the shift and arranged its ordinary standing counterpart later. It changed the order, not the six received hours or the task's scope. Lin learned how often a modest adjustment depended on saying what hurt before it became an incapacity. The keeper did not ask her to diagnose the shoulder. He asked which position she could safely sustain under the clinician's current plan. They wrote the changed order on today's work sheet, where tomorrow's keeper could see that it had been a particular day's arrangement.

lark_e05_after_003.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_003.text: An apprentice carried tea along the stair and left a cup beside the wrong notebook. The cup tipped against a copy of the public freight timetable. Lin lifted the page from the table rather than grasping the falling pot. The apprentice stopped the pot with the tray already beneath it. Nobody needed a burst of qi to save a timetable. Two lower lines blurred beyond use, however, and the receiving keeper replaced the damaged copy from its dated source. Lin kept the ruined sheet aside so nobody would try to improve its missing numbers from memory.

lark_e05_after_004.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_004.text: The apprentice expected a reprimand for the spill and became more upset when the keeper simply assigned cleanup. Lin understood his wish to get the unpleasant part over with. The keeper said he would discuss why the cup had been placed there after the table was dry and the current readers had a sound timetable. At evening, they moved the tea tray's resting place away from the books. The apprentice admitted he had put it near the notebook because that table always looked empty. The future remedy would need to change where tea arrived, not where anger landed.

lark_e05_after_005.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_005.text: Lin's sixth shift was received at its end. Four copper made twenty four in wages for thirty six completed ordinary work hours. The keeper did not pay for the separate invited afternoons as if they had been added to her employment unnoticed. Their receiving belonged to their own agreements. Lin put the day's four copper in her purse and took the work paper to the lodging keeper, who wanted to know whether next week's meal attendance would change with instruction. She could not yet answer before Duan Zhi arrived and accepted the actual practice schedule.

lark_e05_after_006.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_006.text: Her first assessment under the new care allocation took place that evening. The clinician received five copper for a current ordinary examination, leaving thirty five of the assessment portion unspent. He measured comfortable movement without forcing the arm into a position it had not tolerated. There was improvement in one low reach and no improvement in a higher one. Lin preferred the untidy pair of results to a single word such as recovered. The assigned exercises remained gentle. No salve or channel method was offered as a way to erase the tissue's ordinary time.

lark_e05_after_007.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_007.text: The clinician asked whether she slept with the shoulder folded beneath her. She said she sometimes woke that way. He showed her a cloth roll that could discourage the position without strapping her into another one. Lin used a folded piece she already owned, rather than buying a supposedly curative roll from the market. The advice cost her attention at bedtime. It did not consume the treatment material allowance merely because a clinician had named cloth. He marked the next assessment for a fortnight later, or sooner if a new change warranted one.

lark_e05_after_008.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_008.text: Rao Ji passed the clinic door while she was putting her sleeve straight. He had brought a freight worker whose ankle needed an ordinary examination after a misstep. Rao's rank did not let him declare the ankle fit. He waited outside while the worker spoke privately with the clinician. Lin joined him on the low bench. They compared the ordinary difficulty of accepting an altered walking route after an injury. Rao's knee sometimes allowed the direct stair and sometimes refused it. The stair did not respect what a man had demonstrated on his best day.

lark_e05_after_009.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_009.text: Rao asked whether she intended to qualify for six pairs this term. Lin said she intended to practice toward it under the accepted course, with the examination still depending on what she could actually sustain. He disliked the careful answer at first. It sounded to him like a person keeping both success and failure available for later explanation. Lin said she had once preferred a promise whose confidence outran its measurements. Rao considered that. Then he described the day his sixth pair had appeared sound under a familiar task and failed under an unfamiliar ordinary change.

lark_e05_after_010.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_010.text: The examiner on that earlier day had required him to stop. Rao had thought the interruption was humiliation. Weeks later, he could see that the failed movement had not improved while he argued about it. His eventual certificate belonged to a later recovered test, not to the earlier attempt he wished had counted. Lin asked what changed his mind. He said an ordinary apprentice had repeated the examiner's question without knowing it was an insult in his ears. He could answer a boy more honestly than he could answer a man who seemed to hold his future.

lark_e05_after_011.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_011.text: The injured worker came out with a rest plan and an ordinary return date. Rao accompanied him down the gentler stair. He did not offer to carry him simply because six pairs could make some tasks easier. The worker could walk within the clinician's current limits, and being carried over the narrow turns would have made a different problem. Lin watched them until the bend hid the cane. The comparison with her own next pair stayed less grand than she had expected: a stopped task, a changed mind, an apprentice asking a question.

lark_e05_after_012.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_012.text: At supper, Qin's household argued over the first shelf in the shrine room. The nephew had finally named a carpenter, who had a morning free before the next freight departure. Shan Fang wanted the shelf low enough for seated people to reach. The keeper wanted the baskets out of the dampest part of the wall. Qin proposed a height that satisfied neither demand and earned two simultaneous explanations. Lin ate while they negotiated a lower shelf set slightly forward from the stone. The carpenter would still need to accept the actual drawing and price.

lark_e05_after_013.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_013.text: The child's name was Qin Yi. She told Lin this because she disliked being called the person who drew a turnip hound whenever adults had forgotten her name. Lin apologized, asked how Qin Yi preferred her name written, and used it in her next sentence. Qin Yi had a new drawing of the shrine room, complete with a shelf long enough to hold every winter coat in the market. She said scale was a restriction invented by carpenters. Shan Fang said carpenters could enjoy that reputation after agreeing to bring their own wood. Nobody promised the drawing a real building.

lark_e05_after_014.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_014.text: Qin Yi asked Lin whether a seventh pair would let her reach the shelf more easily. Lin told her she did not have a sixth pair yet, and a higher shelf would still need a sound stool or a different shelf. Qin Yi considered this a poor reward for all the adults' attention to cultivation. Qin said she could complain to the shelf. It was already becoming more qualified than the people designing it. Lin found herself laughing at a ladder she had spent years treating as if every rung must also make the world more accommodating.

lark_e05_after_015.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_015.text: After supper, Shan Fang asked Lin to read a private family letter in a corner away from the child. The request included the part she wanted read and the part she wanted left folded. Her sister had offered a winter visit if work could be arranged at the lower market. Shan Fang needed to know whether that was a fixed offer of employment or only a suggestion to ask a stall owner. The letter contained the suggestion. She would have to write again before telling her sister to spend money on the road.

lark_e05_after_016.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_016.text: Lin read the offered passage twice, keeping the folded part untouched. Shan Fang laughed at herself for having heard the promise she wanted instead of the one written. Her sister's visit mattered because they had not spent a whole quiet week together in years. A false employment assurance could buy that week at the cost of a difficult return journey. Lin suggested asking what days the sister could afford without wages, then seeking work within that actual interval. Shan Fang said she would ask her sister first rather than turn the sister into a staffing plan.

lark_e05_after_017.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_017.text: Chen met Lin on the public stair later, returning from a supplier supper he had found dull. His client had heard the comparison's ordinary public decision and was negotiating the next competent step with Hu Lan. He did not ask Lin to alter whatever record she had received or written. Instead, he wanted to know where a visitor could buy a winter buckle that would not turn green at its first wet day. Lin directed him to the woman whose stall sold fewer ornaments than repairs. He seemed grateful for a question with a modest answer.

lark_e05_after_018.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_018.text: They walked only as far as the shared landing. Chen asked whether the mountain had begun to feel like a place she lived rather than a place she had arrived. Lin thought about the tea tray, the child correcting her name, and a week's cloth washed in the same basin. She said the change had occurred somewhere beneath the larger invitations. It was happening even on days when she did not get nearer a sixth pair. Chen said he knew that feeling best when a shopkeeper stopped explaining the local prices to him.

lark_e05_after_019.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_019.text: He carried a small concern he had not raised at the appendix meeting. If his client sold a fitting, the client might later prefer a comparison that sounded uncomplicated. Chen had accepted payment to present its case, not to write a false account. Lin asked whether his fee depended on the sale. It did not. That removed one pressure without removing all of them. He would still need future employment and a reputation for useful negotiations. He was choosing the plain defect record while it could make his next request harder.

lark_e05_after_020.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_020.text: Lin had no flawless advice for that risk. She said she would remember that he had left the loosened screw visible at the first meeting. Chen looked amused that a screw had become her measure of his conduct. He said she could remember the whole sample as well. They separated at the landing, each with an ordinary route to finish alone. The conversation left her more attached to him and less tempted to claim he had no interested loyalties. Friendship had made his difficult honest answer easier to see; it had not removed the difficulty.

lark_e05_after_021.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_021.text: Back at the lodging, Lin found a letter from the mountain desk that had received her original invitation. It named the actual receiving contact for the source material already brought into this term and asked her to close that temporary handoff before formal instruction began. Whatever earlier route had put an example in her application, the old local keepers needed to know where its limited use ended. The notice did not ask her to report an outcome she had not chosen. She put it beside tomorrow's list and planned to answer through the corresponding receiving record.

lark_e05_after_022.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_022.text: Another envelope carried Duan Zhi's travel confirmation. He would arrive by the lower road after his existing grounding bed duty had a named qualified substitute. His knee made the final stair's load schedule unsuitable, so he had accepted the ordinary chair carrier service paid from his own already earned teaching purse. The confirmation named the arrival time rather than promising an immediate lesson. Lin had a new question for him about the order of tasks. She wrote it down and left room beneath it for an answer she could not yet supply.

lark_e05_after_023.speaker: narrator
lark_e05_after_023.text: The lodging keeper extinguished the common room lamp at its usual hour. Lin went upstairs before she could turn tomorrow's practical list into a prediction of her whole life. Her cloth roll was where the clinician had shown her to place it. The window latch caught on the second attempt. Beneath the floor, a guest muttered at a bootlace that had snapped too late for shopping. The market settled through such small dissatisfactions. Lin lay down with six shifts received, one set of chosen afternoons behind her, and another person's actual arrival still ahead.
